name: Svelte

hook.title: Keep your stores. Move components to TSX.
hook.lede: `@pyreon/svelte-compat` runs the Svelte APIs your code imports, `svelte/store` plus lifecycle, context and events, on Pyreon's engine. It is not a `.svelte` compiler: components become TSX, and the store modules they share keep their imports.

covers: `svelte/store`: `writable`, `readable`, `derived`, `readonly`, `get`, with Svelte's lazy start and stop and its equality check.
doesNotCover: The `.svelte` compiler: single-file components, rune syntax (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`), `$:` statements and `$store` auto-subscription.
`onDestroy` (and an `onMount` cleanup) also fires when a parent re-renders, not only on real unmount.
`beforeUpdate` / `afterUpdate` run after the first render only, not on every update.
`getAllContexts()` returns an empty `Map`; `createEventDispatcher` reaches the direct parent only, with no bubbling.
The `create-zero` scaffold has no Svelte option; set the plugin up by hand.

config.note: Types and the JSX runtime come from the compat package.

ports.title: What stays: your stores

before.label: Svelte store module

after.label: Same file on svelte-compat

ports.note: No edits: the alias does the work, and the store contract (`subscribe`, `set`, `update`) behaves like Svelte's.

ports.title: What moves: components

before.label: Svelte 5
before.code:
<script lang="ts">
  let { step }: { step: number } = $props()
  let count = $state(0)
  const doubled = $derived(count * 2)
</script>

<button class="counter" onclick={() => (count += step)}>{count} / {doubled}</button>

after.label: Pyreon

ports.note: Prefer writing `count++`? Plain Mode (`'use plain'`) keeps that style and compiles it to signals.
